key_insight: dLI-RADS achieved 80% lesion-level accuracy versus 74% for LI-RADS and met the study’s non-inferiority criterion in internal evaluation.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support more consistent assessment of small liver lesions on multiphase CT, where LI-RADS imaging features can be difficult to judge.
method: Analyzes manually segmented liver lesions on multiphase CT.
Combines neural network predictions with handcrafted measurements reflecting LI-RADS major features.
Uses logistic regression to estimate hepatocellular carcinoma probability.
evidence_signal: This multicenter retrospective study excluded lesions larger than 40 mm and assessed internal accuracy using 10,000-repetition bootstrap non-inferiority tests with a 5% margin (p = 0.04).
watch_item: Manual segmentation limits workflow automation, and the provided abstract excerpt does not report external-test results.
paper_title: An interpretable deep learning method for early hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase CT
